A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAV2vec research and contain readable main text, equations, six figures, fourteen tables, and Appendices A-C. The material supports a reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-recognition experiments on LRS3 and LRS2, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including the main benchmark tables and the appendix evaluations of unimodal recognition, initialization, and corrupted-data pretraining.

M1.justification: The CAV2vec architecture, teacher-student updates, cross-modal ACP/VCP tasks, masking procedure, and combined loss remain unchanged in Sections 3-4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LRS3 and LRS2 evaluations, VoxCeleb2-based pretrained initialization, the same audio and visual corruption sources, and the appendix ASR/VSR scenarios. No dataset, task, or test environment is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain V-CAFE, RAVEn, BRAVEn, AV-HuBERT, AV-data2vec, and AV-RelScore, with unchanged experiment-specific subsets. Their implementation descriptions in Appendix A.1 also match.

E3.justification: Data processing, training budgets, model sizes, corruption sampling, and WER/N-WER evaluation procedures are unchanged. This includes the five SNR settings and DEMAND evaluation protocol in Appendix A.3.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same task-design ablations, corruption-ratio and loss-weight sensitivity studies, modality-gap visualizations, initialization comparisons, and corrupted-pretraining analyses in Section 5.3 and Appendices B-C.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and averages across evaluation conditions. Neither adds repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains CAV2vec average N-WER values of 5.1%, 5.2%, and 5.1% for object occlusion plus noise, hands occlusion, and pixelated faces, respectively.

T1.justification: The corruption definitions, representation notation, and loss formulations in Equations (1)-(5) are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about corrupted prediction, cross-modal alignment, robustness, and generalization to unseen corruptions. The added code-availability sentence does not change the core contributions.

C2.justification: Explanations of cross-modal alignment and task redundancy, the clean-versus-corrupted performance tradeoff, and resource constraints on pretraining remain unchanged, including the discussion in Appendix C.6.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit CAV2vec code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged, as does the reproducibility statement's planned checkpoint release. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier AVSR methods remain unchanged. Bibliography repagination and colored citations do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a funding acknowledgments section and the abstract's code sentence, and changes the affiliation from 'Department of Electrical Engineering' to 'School of Electrical Engineering.' The scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 colors citations, internal cross-references, and URLs, and slightly reflows the opening pages and bibliography. Figure 1 shifts vertically, while all six figures and fourteen tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The new CAV2vec code link provides useful access information missing from v1, while funding acknowledgments improve disclosure. These are limited documentation improvements: the scientific evidence and conclusions are unchanged, and the supplied PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
